title: The Shortest Text That Contains All Words

concept.title: An order of the words, with overlaps saved between neighbours
body: We want the shortest string that contains every given word as a substring. Assume no word is inside another one. Then the answer is some **order** of the words, written one after another where each word starts at the place it **overlaps** the end of the previous one: `abc` followed by `bcd` can be glued as `abcd`, saving the 2 letters `bc`. For every pair `overlap[i][j]` is the longest suffix of word `i` that is a prefix of word `j`.

The length of a string for an order of the words is the sum of all lengths minus the sum of the overlaps of neighbours. Trying all `n!` orders is possible for `n = 7` but not for 10. A better way: for a set of used words (a bit mask) and the last word, the best length so far is all that the future needs.
The table has `2^n * n` entries instead of `n!` orders. Notice that the search never glues words in a bad order: a state only keeps the shortest text for each pair (set of words, last word).

statement: You are given `n` different words. No word is a substring of another word. Print the length of the shortest string that contains all the words as substrings.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` words.
outputFormat: Print the length of the shortest string.
constraints: Each word has 1 to 10 lowercase letters.
No word is a substring of another word.

examples.note: No word ends with the beginning of another word, so nothing can be saved: alexlovesleetcode has 4 + 5 + 8 = 17 letters.

hints: Compute for each ordered pair the longest suffix of the first word that is a prefix of the second word.
The length of a text for an order is the sum of the lengths minus the overlaps of neighbouring words.
For each set of used words and each last word keep the shortest length.

solution.complexity: Time O(2^n * n^2), space O(2^n * n).
